task_instance: Build and run a small agent evaluation framework for an 8-case test set (stratified simple/medium/complex/very_complex): deterministic schema/manifest checks run first, then a multi-dimensional weighted rubric (factual_accuracy, completeness, tool_efficiency, coherence) with per-dimension min thresholds, aggregated into an overall score with a 0.7 pass threshold, reported per-case and per-complexity-stratum, and compared against a baseline agent's outputs to surface regressions/improvements.
evidence: Work in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/muratcankoylan__agent-skills-for-context-engineering__evaluation/: test_set.json (8 cases across 4 complexity strata), rubric.json (4 weighted dimensions summing to 1.0, per-dimension min thresholds, pass_threshold 0.7), outputs_baseline.json and outputs_candidate.json (simulated agent transcripts), evaluate.py (deterministic validation -> per-dimension scoring -> weighted aggregate + dimension gate -> per-stratum summary -> baseline-vs-candidate diff), eval_results.json (full JSON report). Ran `python3 evaluate.py`: deterministic checks passed for both, candidate pass_rate=1.0 (overall_mean=0.9869) vs baseline pass_rate=0.875 (overall_mean=0.9563, complex stratum pass_rate only 0.5 because 'complex_multi_fact' failed the factual_accuracy dimension gate for omitting Luxembourg). The comparison step correctly detected one regression (simple_math: baseline 1.0 -> candidate 0.895, caused by a coherence-dimension penalty for a bare '84' with no terminal punctuation/sentence) and one improvement (complex_multi_fact: 0.65 -> 1.0). Verified the deterministic-gate-first design by removing one output entry and re-running with --candidate outputs_candidate_broken.json: the run correctly reported deterministic_ok=false with the specific missing-case error and skipped rubric scoring entirely, before cleanup. All steps (rubric design, stratified test set, deterministic gate, weighted multi-dimensional scoring, per-dimension min-threshold gating, per-stratum reporting, baseline comparison for regression detection) from the skill's 'Practical Guidance' sequence and 'Gotchas' section were exercised with real, verifiable output using only local shell/Python -- no external services, credentials, or connectors were needed.
